properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 1:51AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Thursday into the weekend, a series of low pressure systems will
move toward Southeast Alaska, bringing widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall and gale force winds to the Gulf. Strong winds are also
expected for coastal and southern panhandle communities. While the
exact timing and impacts of the system are still being refined,
confidence is continuing to increase that this will be a more
impactful system for Southeast Alaska.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
developing situation and update our forecast.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 13 at 5:36AM EDT until October 15 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Congaree River at Columbia affecting Lexington
and Richland Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Congaree River at Columbia.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 6.5 feet, The lowest parts of the West Columbia
Riverwalk between Gervais Street and SC 12 begin to flood. At 10.0
feet, Flooding occurs on parts of the Cayce and West Columbia
Riverwalk.



* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 11.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 19.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 11.7 feet this morning. It will
then fall to 4.0 feet early Thursday afternoon. It will rise to
4.2 feet early Saturday afternoon. It will then fall again and
remain below flood stage.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 13 at 5:36AM EDT until October 15 at 11:51AM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Congaree River at Congaree NP Near Gadsden
affecting Calhoun and Richland Counties.

Congaree River At Carolina Eastman affecting Calhoun, Lexington and
Richland Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Carolina Eastman.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 115.0 feet, Flooding occurs in low lying areas of the
Carolina Eastman Facility and at the Congaree National Park. At
119.0 feet, Extensive flooding occurs in the Congaree National
Park. Some area farmland is flooded. Minor flooding occurs at the
Carolina Eastman Facility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:04 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 117.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 114.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:04 AM EDT Tuesday was 117.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 119.0 feet
this morning. It will then fall below flood stage late tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 115.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM EDT.

properties.description:

are expected. The strongest winds may be focused immediately
downstream of the higher terrain, and along terrain gaps and
east-west oriented valleys Friday morning.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona.

* WHEN...From 11 PM Thursday to 11 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong and gusty winds over desert areas could result in
blowing dust, briefly lowering visibility below a mile at times.

vehicles traveling along roadways with strong and gusty crosswinds.

may be blown around. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power
outages may result.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 3:41AM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI
properties.description:
Areas of fog have expanded across north-central and northeast
Wisconsin early this morning. The fog was locally dense in
spots, with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less, especially along
the Lake Michigan shoreline from Manitowoc to Door County.

If you have travel plans early this morning, be on alert for
rapidly changing or poor visibilities as low as 1/4 mile or less
in spots. Plan on extra time to reach your destination and allow
extra room between you and the car in front of you.

Visibilities should begin to improve from west to east through
sunrise as a cold front moves across the area.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 13 at 1:31AM MST until October 13 at 8:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, and normally dry washes is
imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 125 AM MST, river gauges on West Clear Creek running into
Verde Lakes and Camp Verde, Fossil Creek, East Verde River, and
the Verde River south of Camp Verde are reporting high flows
which will cause flooding of low water crossings
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Houston Creek, Gap Creek, Bull Run Creek, Pigeon Creek, West
Clear Creek, Cold Water Creek, Chasm Creek, Hardscrabble Creek,
Long Canyon, Fossil Creek, East Verde River, and Verde River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Camp Verde along West Clear Creek, Verde Lakes, Childs Power
Plant, Rockin' River Ranch State Park, Cedar Bench Wilderness,
The Toilet Bowl, Fossil Springs Wilderness, Indian Maiden Falls
and West Clear Creek Wilderness.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Clear Creek Group Campgrounds.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes and waterfalls on Fossil Creek, Bull Pen Day
Use Area, West Clear Creek near the campground, Fossil Creek Dam
"The Toilet Bowl" and Indian Maiden Falls.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.
